claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county was 9.6% above the national level (ratio 1.096, 95% interval 1.058-1.135), about 45.7 more deaths a year than its age structure predicts.
Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county is at 71.1 (three-year mean to 2024) against 73.5 nationally and a target of 80.

Referrals for specialised health care received after processing for more than 21 days, % of the referrals received: Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county is at 1.67 (three-year mean to 2025) against 1 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county is clearly worse than the country is early detection (screening participation).

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 9.2 deaths a year in Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county (range 1.4-18.4) for an assumed EUR 234,297 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 97% of sensitivity runs.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 71.1% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 34% of the gap.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 75.6% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-4.37 percentage points, closing about 69% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
